hits.name: wast3
hits.text:
Anthropic aimed a model at the human cells that stop dividing but refuse to die, and found what keeps them alive.

Nobody asked it for an anti-ageing drug. It was asked what a senescent cell is still building when it has stopped doing everything else.

> READ - the protein output of ageing cells, ribosome activity only, no disease labels
> SORT - what keeps being produced separated from what quietly shuts down
> LINK - each surviving product matched to the signal the cell sends its neighbours
> TEST - the list ranked by which products already have a drug that binds them

A cell that stops dividing is supposed to go quiet. Most of its machinery does exactly that.

A narrow set of production lines stays open. The cell keeps building the molecules that irritate everything around it.

That is the part that ages tissue. Not the dead cells, but the ones still shouting after they stopped working.

The ranking turned up products already targeted by approved drugs, which is the cheapest possible place for a lab to start.

Nothing here clears a treatment. It is a shortlist of what to silence, drawn from data that has been public for years.

Ageing research keeps chasing what cells lose. This looked at what they stubbornly keep making instead.

The ranked product list and the existing drugs that touch it are laid out underneath.
